This Writ Petition is filed under Article 226 of the Constitution of India seeking the following relief:
Kolli Venkateswarlu vs State Of Andhra Pradesh, on 8 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/84456575/
2 ".....pleased to issue an appropriate writ order or direction more particularly one in the nature of writ of mandamus declaring the action of the respondents 3 and 4 and their officials, in threatening to demolish petitioners' tiffin centre bearing Door Nos.28-333 (Assessment No.1131024205) and 28-233 and 28- 33/2 (Assessment Nos.1131024204 and 1131011478) Plot No.37 in D.No.367/1, situated on the northern side of Narasaraopet - Kurnool Road, in Vinukonda Town, Palnadu District, without following due process of law as illegal, arbitrary, violation of principles of natural justice and violative of Articles 14 and 300-A of the Constitution of India and without initiating the procedure as contemplated under the provisions of the A.P. Land Encroachment Act or the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act 2013 and consequently direct the respondents 2 and 3 not to demolish the petitioners' above tiffin centre and not to dispossess the petitioners therefrom without following the due of law and pass....."
2. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioners and the learned Assistant Government Pleader appearing for the respondents.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 3. Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that the petitioners are the absolute owners and possessors of the properties situated in door No.28- 233 in Plot No.37 in D.No.367/1 and an extent of 22.36 square yards in part of Plot No.37, D.No.367/1, situated in Vinukonda Town, Palnadu District.
The subject properties were acquired by the petitioners through a registered sale deed bearing Document Nos.2183/2023 and 2184/2023, dated 13.02.2023.

While so, the respondent authorities, without issuing any notice and without adhering to the provisions of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013,
are trying to interfere with the peaceful possession of the petitioners in respect of the subject properties.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Hence, the Writ Petition.
4. Learned Assistant Government Pleader further submits that the respondents will follow due process of law as contemplated, if they intend to dispossess the petitioners from the subject properties.

5. Having regard to the submissions of the learned counsel for the petitioners, the learned Assistant Government Pleader for the Revenue and on perusal of the material available on record, this Court is of the considered view that the present Writ Petition can be disposed of directing the respondents to follow due process of law, if they intend to dispossess the petitioners from the subject properties.
6. In the result, the Writ Petition is disposed of.
There shall be no order as to costs.
Consequently, Miscellaneous Petitions, if any, pending in the Writ Petition shall stand closed.

VENKATESWARLU NIMMAGADDA, J 08.07.2025 SCH THE HON'BLE SRI JUSTICE VENKATESWARLU NIMMAGADDA WRIT PETITION No.16979 of 2025 08.07.2025 SCH Kolli Venkateswarlu vs State Of Andhra Pradesh, on 8 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/84456575/
